stem:
Victoria is a 3-year-old girl with severe asthma. She is currently taking fluticasone 500 micrograms three times daily. Her mother is worried that increasing the inhaled corticosteroid dose may have harmed Victoria's growth.

What is true about growth-related side effects of inhaled corticosteroids?

options.text: Growth effects of ICSs are not permanent and always reverse when steroids are decreased or stopped
Treatment beginning before puberty is associated with a small (approximately 1cm) reduction in adult height
Growth effects of ICSs are idiosyncratic and may result in increased or decreased growth depending on the child
Growth effects of ICSs are potentially life threatening as children cannot cope with being short
There are no growth effects of ICS

explanation: Inhaled corticosteroids can slightly reduce linear growth velocity, especially when started in prepubertal children, with a small average reduction in adult height of about 1 cm. This effect is modest and must be balanced against the benefit of preventing severe asthma exacerbations.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Part B

rationale: Selected the best existing option because the question asks for a true statement about ICS-related growth effects, and option B is the standard correct statement.

optionExplanations.A: Growth suppression may improve after dose reduction, but it is not accurate to say it always fully reverses.
optionExplanations.B: Correct. Prepubertal exposure is associated with a small reduction in adult height, typically around 1 cm.
optionExplanations.C: ICS effects are not typically described as random increases or decreases in growth.
optionExplanations.D: This is not a recognised description of ICS adverse effects.
optionExplanations.E: ICS can affect growth velocity, particularly at higher doses.

source.questionTextHtml:
Victoria’s mother admits that she has increased the dose of inhaled corticosteroids (ICS) because of her fear that Victoria may have another severe exacerbation.

Victoria’s mother is devastated to think that she may have caused Victoria harm.

What is true about growth related side effects of ICS?

Instructions

Question 1 - 3 relate to this case

Asthma Management: Medications and Devices - Case 1

Victoria is a 3 year old girl with a history of two admissions to the intensive care unit with asthma exacerbations. You are seeing her for the first time. Over the last year she has had only one visit to the emergency department with no exacerbations since your last review. She is currently taking fluticasone (Flixotide) 500 µg three times daily (tds).
